Since the wrapper args are easily added by the user (by using finalAttrs.packpathDirs), I propose we dont set them when wrapRc is set as well.
It's a breaking change for anyone using wrapRc.

twice now, once for the variants, once for the image file name.

fixes #394626

items.content_html:
mptcpd is a daemon that manager mptcp path like ip mptcp do

ip mptcp endpoint add 192.168.1.100 dev eth0 subflow
ip mptcp endpoint add 10.0.0.4 dev wwan0 subflow
ip mptcp limit set subflow 5

Mptcpd can be configured via configFile or command line options, however the default configfile live in /nix/store does not set subflow flags nor detect iface by default. Thus an extra mptcpdFlags option is needed.

The provided example extraMptcpdFlags

        example = [
          "--addr-flags=subflow"
          "--notify-flags=existing,skip_link_local,skip_loopback,check_route"
        ];

is suitable for endpoint router settings and manager mptcp path similar to what the NetworkManager does.

Users can follow the redhet instruction Chapter 35. Getting started with Multipath TCP to test for mptcp.

The motivation for this change is to fix the issue where if you ssh into a NixOS system and then log out the title bar is permanently hosed. Specifically, when you ssh into a NixOS system it will add ${USER}@${HOST} to the title bar, but when you log out of that system the title bar will still have ${USER}@${HOST} afterwards.

The solution I went with is the one described in this StackOverflow answer to reset the title bar using the /etc/bash_logout script, which will then prompt the local shell to restore its own default title bar. That in turn entailed adding a new NixOS option to configure /etc/bash_logout.

Note that /etc/bash_logout is a NixOS-specific thing. Stock Bash doesn't support a global /etc/bash_logout script and only supports user-local ~/.bash_logout scripts but Nixpkgs patches Bash to support /etc/bash_logout, which is why this change works.
